english: But if things go well, after the election he might be up for a promotion.
That'd leave me as First-in-Command.
Sounds like Tolstad would be better with you in charge.
You think you'd do things better?
Sounds like petty bullshit to me.
Thank you, Cleric. How kind of you to say.
The orc gives you a wry smile. "I agree."
She takes a deep breath, looking to the side.
Then she says, "Yes. No doubt."
Your brazen words make her chuckle.
Office intrigue always is.
But don't worry. I'll fix all of that once I'm in charge.
Confident girl.
Woman.
Don't infantilize her.
First of all, who cares? Second of all, please shut the fuck up.
Gods, she's hot.
She throws her entire head back in a fit of laughter.
Oh gods! You truly are a marvel, Cleric.
She mimics wiping a tear from her eyes.
Yeah, I'm funny. Heh.
So you actually don't like him?
You sure are, she says, and gives you a big smile.
Oh. You're not-
No, Cleric.
Can't say. Industry secrets, you know.
She winks a lot, this one.
Be grateful to this woman. She keeps giving you hints that she's quirky.
Quirky! Quirky! Quirky! Quirky!
Shut up!
Sure!
Her eyes widen. "Oh. Oh!"
In pure horror?
She's excited.
It will be fun.
After the election, right?
What do you want to do on the date?
What is a date?
That's enough about the date, for now.
Right.
I'll leave that up to you, Cleric.
What is...
It's a- hold on, do you not know what a date is?
I'm joking, Agent Viira.
Of course I do. I'm checking if you know.
Go on.
Funny.
But just to make sure...
She blinks a few times.
She opens her mouth to speak, then thinks better of it.
You make her nervous.
But less in a 'he's hot' kind of way, and more in an 'I'm standing near an active volcano' kind of way.
A date is a social meeting between two people. With romantic interest.
Okay?
(Gulp.) "Sounds lovely."
I like that.
I knew that.
She pushes a strand of hair behind her ear and gives you another smile.
...Good.
Great! I mean... good.
What else?
I make sure the flow of goods remains efficient and uninterrupted by local shenanigans.
Shenanigans? Ah. She, too, is a dodger of consequences.
I also represent the organization as a member in the Freestrider Party as well. Which makes it a lot more interesting.
Red.
Like blood. She gives you a sinister smile.
She's very charming.
Gods. This woman will be the end of you.
Hm. Why do you ask?
I read in a book once that it's a good question to break the ice.
I'm interested. In you.
Nevermind.
You read?
Don't sound so impressed, orc.
She's mocking you.
But, there's no need to break the ice. We're already talking, Cleric.
Oh! Hm. Right.
She's flustered.
She's trying to ignore your awkward comment.
Nevermind, then.
I did not know my mother. I was born into a Fell Tire JT. A Journeyman Tribe. Where children are raised collectively.
We made scissors. That's my special blood talent. My 'fate', as it were.
I didn't like it in the factory. So I left to Bloodcity Bay.
I joined a warband. A few, actually. Learned to be smart. Eventually ended up in Reeds, where my true talents were recognized.
Orcs are the original factory workers.
Woah, woah... hold on a second.
(Let her continue.)
Hm? What?
...Scissors?
I'm confused. Please elaborate on the special blood.
I didn't ask for your life story, Agent. (Try to get her to skip.)
Too bad!
Oh. I apologize. I should clarify...
Vérôrôkség. Gifted by Blood. Each orcish clan was given a specialty by the Queen-Mother.
My clan's gift was the magical affinity for making amazing scissors.
A working people. Factory people.
That is what the Arcanists used to call orcs.
Every factory in Fell Tire was human-run during the Arcane Era.
The orcs were under terrible oppression.
Super efficient, honestly.
Though being locked down like that sounds like shit. Good thing she left.
That's ridiculous.
That's cool?
Yes. It is.
No. It is not.
The Revolution was already strong when I joined.
So once I'd realized I'd missed all the real action, I ended up taking a job to spread the word.
I spent a season in Vourgeni at first, but I never clicked with the locals.
So Norvik it was.
And now I'm here!
She bows her head in a formal fashion.
Anything else you wanted to ask?
Strong enough.
Oh, this old rag?
The outfit is an AR import. Originally designed by Frukk Framm, I hear...
Although these are obviously just factory knockoffs.
Reliable, though.
Good thing!
And what about you? You holding up alright?
No. (Look sad.)
Yes, I'm doing great.
Don't snoop. It's rude.
Aw. Sad to hear.
Good to hear!
She scoffs loudly, giving you a shocked expression.
Then she shrugs. "Okay?"
She does not care. Not really.
Yes, we are having very wonderful weather today, I agree.
Although it is quite difficult to see it down here on Waterlane. Because of the ceiling.
The weather?
You attempt to woo her, and she is talking about the weather?
Wow. Smooth.
She's avoiding the subject by pretending to not hear what you said.
You make her uncomfortable.
Nonsense. How could you, this puny little man, possibly make such a handsome and towering creature have any type of emotional reaction?
Tell her.
Tell her what you think. What you BELIEVE.
Focus on her.
Do not let her notice it.
Hit her with the perfect line.
I should just give up on this, shouldn't I? I'm no good at flirting.
Yes. The weather. That's what I said. (ABORT. ABORT. MAYBE TRY IT LATER INSTEAD.)
How sad. This poor woman must have trouble with avoidant attachment.
She thinks you are coming on too strong.
Not the time nor place, buddy.
Maybe she missed it?
It would probably be for the best.
This is your only shot at getting her really weak in the legs.
Stern. STERN.
I don't want to flirt.
She squints and crosses her arms.
Then just go along with her weather comment.
Easy way out.
Her expression grows a little concerned.
Alright. Good luck to you. And your potential future descendants who smile upon you through glorious Strings.
She gives you an overly enthusiastic nod.
The perfect line. The perfect... line.
Right. You got this.
I do?
You do.
Just say...
Get to know me, you say?
Figure me out, you say?
She shakes her head, but can't help but let a grin sneak onto her face.
Your insistence is a bit endearing, I'll admit.
So... fine.
A date with this helmed human does sound like a rather memorable night, doesn't it?
Nice job, stud.
The handsome woman is falling for your confidence and stern behavior.
Yes, yes it does.
You'll just have to find out.
The goblin closes his eyes.
In shame.
The orc crosses her arms.
Well then. Now, with that settled...
One step closer to true victory.
I do have some work to do, if you haven't got any more questions?
You've got this. The perfect line is at the tip of your...
Not yet.
Gotta swoon her first.
What?
Oh shit. She's looking at you.
Quick, stall!
But what about that perfect line?
You got nothing, kid. Now SAY SOMETHING!
The orc gives you a polite smile.
Uh, uh...! (Start shaking.)
Cleric. Did you have any questions, or...
Don't lose it!
Be COOL!
The orc crosses her arms and lifts her chin.
This... date, could you... explain to me, what exactly would your plans contain?
No. I've never been on a date.
Her mouth-sound hurts.
Don't say that!
That's the exact opposite thing she likes!
Well, perhaps we can look into that at a later date- I mean, later time then, Cleric.
If that's... okay with you.
(Just nod. Pathetically.)
(Shrug. Confusingly.)
She puts on a fake smile.
So.
No! The crystal, it's-
The instant you cast your spell, a blast of esoteric distortion causes it to fizzle before you.
A counterspell. From where?
You'd really think I'd fall for that twice, did you?
Interesting move.
On the table. Those mineral shards are ingrained with some type of anti-magical energy.
Fascinating.
You've heard of protective magic items before, but this one is clearly beyond your means.
An anti-magic aura.
Please do not cast any spells on AR property, Cleric.
And I will kindly ask you to avoid casting spells on me in general.
Cleric.
The orc sweeps in and places a firm hand on your shoulder.
Please refrain from touching things here. You are a guest. Not in any way admitted to indulge in company property.
She takes a few steps back, shaking her head.
Your <u>EGO</u>.
It is... bruised.
What a firm grip.
Honestly, you should just sneak inside at night instead.
Maybe bribe that weird thing in the fireplace too...
E-How embarrassing.
